name: Umamaheswarar Temple, Konerirajapuram
deity: Shiva as Umamaheswarar, with the goddess Mangalanayaki
period: Great Chola temple of the Kaveri delta, sung in the Tevaram, rebuilt in stone in the 10th century under Sembiyan Mahadevi
summary: At Konerirajapuram, the Tirunallam of the Tevaram, Shiva is Umamaheswarar in a temple rebuilt by the Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi, famed for housing one of the largest and finest Chola bronze Natarajas.

sections.history: Konerirajapuram, called Tirunallam in the Tevaram, is a Shaiva village of the Kaveri delta and a Paadal Petra Sthalam praised by Appar and Thirugnana Sambandar. Its great temple was rebuilt in stone in the tenth century under Sembiyan Mahadevi, the Chola queen whose patronage transformed many delta shrines from brick to stone and left some of the finest work of the age. The Lord is worshipped as Umamaheswarar and the goddess as Mangalanayaki. The temple is renowned among art historians for its sculpture and bronzes, and stands as a monument of the mature early Chola style as much as a living shrine.
sections.architecture: The temple is a classic Chola structure of the tenth century, its sanctum and vimana carrying the restrained, elegant sculpture of the Sembiyan Mahadevi period. The sanctum enshrines the Shiva linga of Umamaheswarar, with the goddess Mangalanayaki in her own shrine. Its most celebrated treasure is a colossal bronze Nataraja, among the largest and finest of all Chola bronzes, housed in a separate enclosure built so that the image cannot be removed without dismantling the structure. Pillared halls and niche figures complete a temple prized for its art.
sections.legends: As Tirunallam the place is praised in the Tevaram, and tradition honours it among the shrines that the saints sang on their pilgrimages through the delta. The temple's identity, however, rests above all on the devotion of Sembiyan Mahadevi, whose rebuilding in stone is remembered as an act of piety, and on the great Nataraja, before whom generations have worshipped the dancing Lord in bronze.
sections.festivals: Arudra Darshan in the Tamil month of Margazhi, the festival of Nataraja's cosmic dance, is kept with special devotion given the temple's famous bronze. Maha Shivaratri, the monthly Pradosham, and the Tamil month festivals are also observed. Festival dates follow the Tamil calendar, so confirm them locally.
sections.experience: Konerirajapuram rewards those who come for Chola art as much as for worship: the great bronze Nataraja in its own enclosure is one of the sights of the delta, and the sculpture of the Sembiyan Mahadevi temple repays a slow round. Set in a quiet village near Kuthalam, it is often visited with the other Tevaram shrines of the Kumbakonam–Mayiladuthurai belt.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Konerirajapuram is near Kuthalam in Mayiladuthurai district, within reach of Kumbakonam and Mayiladuthurai. Kumbakonam and Mayiladuthurai are the nearest railheads; Tiruchirappalli airport is about 100 km away. Local buses and autos reach the village.
